objectClass.primaryType: flat extruded monogram badge (two-letter 'JC' logotype with an accent chevron)
formLanguage: planar profile extruded along the view axis
structureKind: detached accent mark floating in the J counter gap
motionPotential: rigid-body yaw/pitch tilt of the whole badge
independent z-offset of the chevron (parallax accent)
per-part material-state swap for light/dark theme
objectClass.notes: Vector logotype, not a photographed object. Measured from the source PNG: 99.2% of opaque pixels are exactly two colours (#000000 ink, 40.63% of frame; #e48e00 accent, 0.86%); the remainder is anti-aliasing. There is no shading, gradient, grain or wear anywhere in the reference, so albedo is the only observable channel and every surface response below is inference about a physical extruded badge, not measurement of the reference.

reasoning: Two opaque colour regions only; connected-component labelling of the alpha mask gives exactly two ink islands (18485 px 'J', 17905 px 'C') that touch diagonally, plus one 749 px accent island.
Every edge is a straight segment or a circular-arc terminal in one plane: the whole subject is a 2D profile with depth, so silhouette complexity is high but volumetric complexity is near zero.
No occlusion: the reference is an orthographic-equivalent flat elevation, so nothing is hidden except the side walls and back face that extrusion itself defines.
Held at 'simple' because component count, hierarchy depth and material layer count are all minimal; the detail that matters is boundary placement, which is carried by the traced profiles.

specDepthDecision.rationale: Observed structure is two macro solids. Meso/micro levels would be invented, not observed: the hairline slits and rounded counter are boundary features OF the letters profile, not separate parts, so they are authored as localFeatures on the letters component and as vertices in its traced contour.

detailInventory.note: Zones scanned with forge/stage1_intake/build_detail_inventory.py (component-zones: letters-stem, chevron, letters-top-arm, c-bowl-left). Every detail below is linked to a component localFeature or a material localOverride.

details.description: Three vertical transparent hairlines cut through the ink at x=158-161 px (4 px wide, y 0-70), x=171-174 px (4 px, y 0-70 and y 140-209) and x=188-191 px (3 px, full height). They are what separates the J stem from the C bowl; losing them merges the two letterforms into one slab.
details.measurement: slit widths 2-4 px at 417 px reference width = 0.010-0.019 model units

details.description: The J counter is a vertical slot with semicircular terminals, open to the background on both flanks between y=70 and y=140 px. Its rounded ends (radius ~12 px) are the single most identity-defining curve in an otherwise orthogonal mark.
details.measurement: slot x 118-142 px, y 30-180 px; terminal radius ~12 px = 0.057 model units

details.description: The C opens to the right: its upper and lower terminals are cut back on a near-vertical shear, leaving a right-facing aperture. The bowl interior is a stadium-shaped negative space, not a circle.
details.measurement: aperture spans y 0-30 px and y 175-209 px on the right flank of the C

details.description: The accent is a downward-pointing chevron with a concave notch in its top edge and a blunt apex; it reads as a check/tick rather than a triangle.
details.measurement: 48 x 27 px bounding box at x 68-115, y 106-132 px

details.description: Inferred, not observed: on a physical extruded badge the side walls catch the key light at a different angle to the front cap, so the profile boundary reads as a thin lighter/darker rim. Carried as a material localOverride on the side-wall face set.
details.measurement: wall height = extrusion depth 0.12 model units (letters) / 0.05 (chevron)

anatomy.note: Only meaningful when objectClass.primaryDomain is character or hybrid. Set applies=true and fill from forge/stage1_intake/extract_landmarks.py. See grimoire/character/reconstruction.md and grimoire/character/likeness_maximization.md.

resolvedUnknowns.unknown: Extrusion depth is not observable from a single flat vector view.
resolvedUnknowns.resolution: Authored as 0.12 unit for the letters solid and 0.05 unit for the chevron (12% and 5% of the logo height). Recorded in assumptions and risks/depth-unobservable.

resolvedUnknowns.unknown: Side-wall and back-face treatment (straight wall vs chamfer) is unobservable.
resolvedUnknowns.resolution: Straight wall, bevelEnabled:false, so the front elevation stays pixel-faithful to the reference. Recorded in assumptions.

resolvedUnknowns.unknown: Whether the chevron is a detached piece or printed on a shared backplate.
resolvedUnknowns.resolution: Modelled as a detached solid standing 0.045 unit proud of the letter front cap, per the stated badge design intent. Recorded in assumptions and in the chevron/chevron-stand-proud local feature.

definitionOfDone: The rendered model matches the reference silhouette, primary proportions, visible component hierarchy, material response, and most recognizable local features for the selected fidelity tier.

featureGroups.name: Overall silhouette and proportions
qualityCriteria: Bounding shape, dominant curves, negative spaces, and scale relationships are explicitly described.
failureModes: model reads as a generic placeholder instead of the reference object
major proportions are guessed without evidence

featureGroups.name: Primary structure and hierarchy
qualityCriteria: Major parts, joints, seams, contact points, and parent-child relationships are named before code generation.
failureModes: large visible parts are merged into one mesh
component hierarchy is too shallow for the observed complexity

featureGroups.name: Attachment and joint correctness
qualityCriteria: Every visible child appendage, branch, limb, handle, connector, tube, cable, horn, wing, leg, or hinged part has an attachment contract with parent socket, localStart/localEnd, contact type, embed/overlap, and gap tolerance.
failureModes: child part root floats away from the parent
branch/limb/tube is centered in space instead of pivoting from its root
parent-child transform mixes world and local coordinates

featureGroups.name: Surface material response
qualityCriteria: Albedo zones, roughness, normal/bump/displacement intent, cavity dirt, edge wear, and local overrides are specified where visible.
Important materials define independent albedo, roughness, height/normal, and AO responses instead of reusing one texture for unrelated PBR channels.
Surface response is decomposed into macro, meso, and micro frequency bands with scale and amplitude tied to object scale.
failureModes: local material variation is missing or not tied to image evidence

featureGroups.name: Reference color, material, and lighting response
qualityCriteria: Material-pass names the reference-derived albedo palette, roughness variation, tactile normal/bump/displacement response, and local masks.
When a source image is available, run reference PBR extraction and require confidence >= 0.7 before treating maps as implementation-ready.
Lighting-pass names key/fill/rim or environment light, exposure, tone mapping, background, and contact shadow behavior.
Neutral, grazing-angle, and reference-matched renders prove that surface relief survives relighting and is not painted into albedo.
failureModes: model has acceptable shape but reads as flat shaded or plastic
colors are a generic average instead of reference-observed local color zones
lighting is evenly ambient and cannot reproduce the source value range

visualDeltaChecks: local feature placement and scale delta
antiShallowSpecRules: Do not proceed to code if qualityContract.qualityBar is unassessed.
Do not proceed to code if the spec only contains a root component for a moderate or complex object.
Do not proceed to code if required featureGroups are not represented by componentTree, materials, or repetitionSystems.
Do not proceed to code if visible local features are described only in prose and not attached to components/materials/evidenceRefs.
Do not proceed past structural-pass if attached child parts lack attachment.parentSocket, localStart, localEnd, embedDepth/overlap, and gapTolerance.
Do not pass material look-dev when albedo is reused as roughness, height, normal, or AO.
Do not pass material look-dev without macro, meso, and micro surface frequency bands for close-up materials.
Do not pass reference-fidelity material look-dev from a source image without usable referencePbr maps or an explicit documented limitation.
Do not patch a spec with extracted PBR maps when extraction confidence is below the target threshold unless the user explicitly accepts lower fidelity.
Do not place adjacent separate-geometry parts below 0.02 world-unit seam overlap (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).
Do not satisfy raised or recessed relief, fasteners, or grip structure with a map alone when the feature affects form; use geometry or displacement (source: grimoire/build/geometry_patterns.md).

authoringInstruction: Fill observed object class, complexity reasoning, featureGroups, visualDeltaChecks, and unknowns before generating or implementing ObjectSculptSpec.
